mainTopic: Why both the משנה here and the משנה in עבודה זרה are needed, and why forbidden animals mixed with other animals are not בטל ברוב
overview: The גמרא explains why we need two משניות that both say a forbidden animal mixed with other animals does not get cancelled by the majority. One is the משנה here, which is about קדשים. The other is the משנה in עבודה זרה, which is about חולין. With קדשים we might have been lenient to avoid a loss to the Temple. With חולין we might have been lenient because nothing disgusting is being offered to ה׳. So both are needed. The גמרא then asks why the forbidden animals are not simply בטל ברוב. One possible answer is that animals are חשיבי, too important to be cancelled. That answer works for the view that reads the rule as 'כל שדרכו לימנות', but not for the view that reads it as 'את שדרכו לימנות'. The גמרא then begins quoting the משנה in ערלה where this argument comes from, about bundles of תלתן that are כלאי הכרם, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both משניות are needed: the first reason
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the משנה in עבודה זרה, we might think the strict rule applies only to ordinary animals, and not to קדשים, where it would cause a loss to the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we learned this only from there, I would have said it applies to an ordinary person. But for the Most High, I might say we should not lose all the animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we need both the משנה here and the one in עבודה זרה. This step gives the first half: why the משנה here is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in עבודה זרה is about a mixture that becomes forbidden to a הדיוט, a regular person. When קדשים are involved, forbidding the whole mixture means a loss to גבוה, the Temple. So we might have said that in that case we should be lenient, so as not to ruin all the good קרבנות. Our משנה teaches that even then, the whole mixture is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are needed; neither teaching is extra
I would have thought (a mistaken first thought)
An ordinary person; non-holy use
The Most High; things belonging to the Temple
We should cause them to be lost

steps.confusionAlert: צריכי does not mean the two משניות argue with each other. They agree. The גמרא is only showing that each one teaches something we could not have learned from the other.

phrases.english: Both are needed; for if [we learned it only] from there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה in עבודה זרה about forbidden things mixed with ordinary animals.

phrases.english: I would have said: [it applies only] to an ordinary person,
but for the Most High, I might say
we should not cause all of them to be lost;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of why two משניות teach the same rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each source is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For קדשים, we would not forbid the whole mixture, to avoid a loss to the Temple.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה teaches that even with קדשים, the whole mixture is forbidden.

steps.title: Both משניות are needed: the second reason
steps.stepSummary: If we only had our משנה, we might think the strict rule applies only to קדשים, because offering something from such a mixture is disgusting. With חולין there is no such reason, so we might have let איסורי הנאה be בטל ברוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we learned it only from here, I would have said this applies to קדשים, because it is disgusting. But with חולין, which is not disgusting, I might say that things forbidden for benefit become cancelled in a majority. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the explanation: why the משנה in עבודה זרה is needed too. It then closes with 'צריכא': both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה might be strict only because bringing a קרבן from a mixed-up group that includes a forbidden animal is מאיס, disgusting before ה׳. With ordinary animals that are only forbidden for benefit, nothing disgusting is happening. So we might have used the normal rule of ביטול ברוב. The משנה in עבודה זרה teaches that even there, there is no ביטול.

keyTerms.meaning: Disgusting, repulsive (unfit to offer to ה׳)
Holy offerings
Ordinary, non-holy things
Things one may not get any benefit from
Let them be cancelled out by the majority

steps.whatToRemember: Each משנה has its own reason it might have been lenient. For קדשים: avoiding a loss to the Temple. For חולין: there is nothing disgusting about it. So both are needed to teach that there is no ביטול in either case.

phrases.english: And if [we learned it only] from here, I would have said:
this applies only to sacrificial animals, because it is repulsive,
but non-sacred animals, which are not repulsive,
I might say: items forbidden for benefit
should be nullified in a majority; [therefore] both are needed.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling. Both mean 'let them be nullified'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each source is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For חולין, where nothing is disgusting, the forbidden animals would be בטל ברוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה in עבודה זרה teaches that even with חולין, there is no ביטול.

steps.title: Why aren't the forbidden animals cancelled by the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the basic rule: normally a minority of forbidden items is בטל ברוב, so why not here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them be cancelled out by the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the rule itself. Why don't the few forbidden animals just become cancelled by the many permitted ones?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In most of הלכה, a small amount of something forbidden mixed into a larger amount of permitted things loses its status. That is ביטול ברוב. The גמרא asks why animals should be any different.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them be nullified (a challenge)
Majority

phrases.english: But let them be nullified in a majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing both משניות are needed, the גמרא questions the rule they both teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of both משניות that a mixture of animals is entirely forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule of ביטול ברוב should cancel the minority of forbidden animals.

steps.title: A suggested answer: animals are too important to be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: One could answer that animals are חשיבי, important items, which are not cancelled. That works for the view that the rule is 'כל שדרכו לימנות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say they are important and are not cancelled, that works well for the one who says the משנה reads 'כל שדרכו לימנות', anything that is sometimes counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer: animals are important, so they don't get cancelled. It admits this answer works, but only for one opinion. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things that are sold one by one are considered חשוב, important, and are not בטל. One view reads the משנה as 'כל שדרכו לימנות', anything that is sometimes sold by count. Animals are sometimes sold one at a time, so for this view they count as important and are not cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introducing a possible answer)
They are important
This works out well (but only for some)
Anything that is sometimes sold by count

phrases.english: And if you would say: they are significant and are not nullified,
this works out well according to the one who says:
'Any item whose manner is to be counted' is what we learned;
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה in ערלה about which items are too important to be nullified, quoted in the next steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the question of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested answer that works for only one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals should be בטל ברוב like other mixtures.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals are חשיבי and are not cancelled, at least according to the view of 'כל שדרכו לימנות'.

steps.title: The answer fails for the other opinion
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the rule is 'את שדרכו לימנות', only things that are always sold by count, animals do not qualify. So the question returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the משנה reads 'את שדרכו לימנות', the item that is always counted, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the 'important item' answer does not work for the second opinion. So why are the animals not cancelled for that view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this view, only something that is always sold by count is important enough to avoid ביטול. Animals are sometimes sold as a whole herd, so they would not count as important. That brings back the question of step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Only an item that is always sold by count
What can be said? (there seems to be no answer)

steps.confusionAlert: The two readings differ by one word: כל ('any item') versus את ('the item'). That small word decides whether animals count as 'important'.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
'An item whose manner is to be counted' is what we learned,
phrases.notes: For this view, the item must always be sold by count, not just sometimes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 4 and reopens the question of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that animals are חשיבי and not cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under 'את שדרכו לימנות', animals are not always counted, so they are not important and should be בטל ברוב.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה where the argument appears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה in ערלה about someone who had bundles of תלתן that were כלאי הכרם. That is the source of the 'counted items' argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Someone who had bundles of fenugreek that were forbidden mixtures of the vineyard...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the source משנה to show where the argument between 'כל' and 'את' comes from. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תלתן grown together with grapes in a vineyard becomes כלאי הכרם, which is forbidden for benefit. This משנה will discuss whether such bundles can be cancelled in a mixture. Its wording is the basis for the two readings mentioned above.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundles
Fenugreek, a kind of legume
Forbidden mixtures planted in a vineyard, forbidden for benefit

phrases.english: As we learned: One who had
bundles of fenugreek of diverse kinds of the vineyard,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in ערלה 3:6–7, and the quote keeps going after this line.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִּילְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cites the source of the two readings mentioned in steps 4 and 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the משנה about bundles of תלתן that are כלאי הכרם, the source of the debate over which items are too important to be cancelled.
